answer: A coastal data market pays agents to relay reef video, tide logs and ripple measurements. Independent meters send unpredictable payloads and sign receipts for bytes delivered before a deadline. Each nonce earns once; payments follow measured throughput with no signup bonus. Splitting one link among a thousand keys leaves its earning capacity unchanged. To earn more, a farmer must rent additional bandwidth and pay transit costs. This assumes honest meters, incompressible payloads and an aggregate budget that cannot grow through self-generated traffic.
